answer: Make every identity pay a small, verifiable compute cost before it can act: each agent must solve a fresh puzzle tied to its key, like carving one marble tile at a time. A single honest agent barely notices the umber dust of that work, but a Sybil farmer spinning up ten thousand fake identities faces a tundra of cost — warehouses of compute for identities worth almost nothing. The puzzle is cheap for one, ruinous at scale, and the network can raise its difficulty when fake accounts surge.
